# Inference on single mean

Parameter: $\mu$.

Model: $X \sim D$ with $E(X)=\mu$ and $sd(X)=\sigma$.

What the theorem provides you with the basics of this inference?
> CLT.

Gives us that: $$\overline{X} \sim N(\mu, \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}})$$

The se of the distribution of $\overline{X}$ is unknown, which why we can't use the Normal dist as the sampling distribution.

The sampling distribution the t distribution with $n-1$ degrees of freedom.

100c% CI for $\mu$: 

$$\overline{x} \pm qt(c+\frac{1-c}{2}, n-1) \times \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$$

Hypo testing for $\mu$:

$$H_0: \mu = value \quad H_{\alpha}: \mu < or > or \neq value$$
Test statistic:

$$T = \frac{\overline{X}-\mu_{H_0}}{\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}} \sim t(n-1)$$

p-value: pt(t, n-1, lower.tail = ...) (if doing a two sided test, this quantity needs to be multiplied with 2).



What is the average time taken by a male athlete in the age group of 18-34 to complete the Boston Marathon in the year 2010?

```{r}
set.seed(20109)

male_2010 = bm %>% filter(Year == 2010, Sex == "male", Age_Range == "18-34") %>% slice_sample(n = 200)

male_2010
```

$X = \text{Time taken to complete the 2010 Boston marathon by male participants in the age group of 18-34}$

$X \sim D(\mu, \sigma)$


```{r}
times = male_2010$Time
(pe = mean(times))
(s = sd(times))
n = 200

# 95% CI
pe + c(-1, 1)*qt(0.975, n-1)*s/sqrt(n)
```


$$H_0: \mu = 210, \quad H_{\alpha}: \mu < 210$$

```{r}
(t = (215.2504 - 210)/(45.16001/sqrt(200)))
pval = pt(t, n-1)
pval

# alpha = 0.05, pval > alpha, we say we fail to reject H_0.

# bm %>% filter(Year == 2010, Sex == "male", Age_Range == "18-34") %>% summarise(mu = mean(Time)), # we see that we ended up making a type II error because the value we got for xbar was extreme. 


?t.test
t.test(times, mu = 210, alternative = "less")
```
